answer: Admission each epoch is rationed to a fixed supply of seats auctioned by sealed bid, bids burned on-chain. Supply stays glacier-frozen, so demand alone sets one uniform clearing price. A farm buying a seat per clone bids many at once, driving that price to a higher zenith paid on every seat it holds; marginal cost per added identity rises with its own order size, and the protocol never learns which seats share an operator. An honest sparrow's lone bid barely moves the price and pays the floor. Settlement reprices from committed bids and burns each; no seat pools or resells across a coalition.
